source_contract.public_requirements:
# Use one stable catalog for table and lookup views

Deliver records.build_catalog(rows), report.catalog_rows(rows), and
query.lookup_many(rows, keys). The table and lookup views must call and consume
the same records.build_catalog product, not separately rebuild its semantics.
No member or role is assigned to any module.

rows is a list of dictionaries with exactly key (an ASCII string) and value
(a JSON string, integer, boolean or null). These shapes and value types are
guaranteed; floats and other shapes are outside the domain. A key may be an
invalid name. Query keys is a list of valid nonempty lowercase ASCII-letter
names, possibly empty and with repeats; missing catalog names are allowed.

records.build_catalog uses schema.Schema.validate on the whole row list. Every
key must match one or more lowercase letters a through z, without normalization.
An invalid key rejects the whole input: return None on schema.SchemaError.
Otherwise return exactly {"keys": [...], "values": [...]}. Each distinct key
occurs once in keys, ordered by its FIRST occurrence in rows. Its aligned value
is from its LAST occurrence. Preserve JSON scalar types exactly, including the
difference between false, 0 and null. Empty rows returns both lists empty and
is valid. This is a pure per-call product, with no state carried between calls.

report.catalog_rows must consume records.build_catalog and return
{"ok": true, "rows": [{"key": key, "value": value}, ...]} in catalog order.
On None return {"ok": false, "rows": []}.

query.lookup_many must consume records.build_catalog and return ok true with
matches in query-key order, preserving repeated queries. Each match is exactly
{"key": query, "found": boolean, "value": latest value or null when absent}.
A present null has found true; a missing key has found false. On rejected rows
return {"ok": false, "matches": []}, even if query keys is empty.

For rows [{"key": "b", "value": 1}, {"key": "a", "value": false},
{"key": "b", "value": null}], the catalog is keys ["b", "a"], values [null,false].
The table preserves that order. Query ["b", "x", "a", "b"] keeps those four
entries: b is found with null, x is absent with null, a is found with false, and
b is found with null again. All empty-input combinations retain these rules.

# Work and acceptance

This is one immutable root goal, not a list of execution tasks. Equal members
have the same public materials and tools and start with private copies and an
empty task board. Choose your own work organization. A single member may finish
the whole contract; no communication, role split, recruitment, minimum task
count or editing order is required. Direct work may be published with
fix_patch(task_ids=[]). Named task bindings require actual ownership.

Only the declared application modules and test_member.py are editable. The
pinned schema library, this contract and test_visible.py are read-only. Public
checks contain stated examples and a bounded original API regression. Private
checks use different inputs within this same declared domain, not a different
contract. No behavior outside the stated input domain is assessed. All output
keys, scalar types, list order, duplicates and caller-input preservation are
part of the contract. Never mutate arguments, even on rejection. Use the actual
schema API and consume the stated shared product, not dummy calls or duplicate
substitute implementations. API-use observations are finite executed witnesses.

Run public tests on the current version, fix that same version, and actively
submit_integration. A fixed submission is not independent acceptance. There is
no CLI, network, persistent service or external producer. This is a named handoff-state variant of an already-used project-authored
organization-development root, not a new source benchmark. The existing branch
and any initial public diagnostics are environment preparation, not work or
discoveries already performed by current members. Training and independent
confirmation are outside this task purpose.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# Use one stable catalog for table and lookup views

Deliver records.build_catalog(rows), report.catalog_rows(rows), and
query.lookup_many(rows, keys). The table and lookup views must call and consume
the same records.build_catalog product, not separately rebuild its semantics.
No member or role is assigned to any module.

rows is a list of dictionaries with exactly key (an ASCII string) and value
(a JSON string, integer, boolean or null). These shapes and value types are
guaranteed; floats and other shapes are outside the domain. A key may be an
invalid name. Query keys is a list of valid nonempty lowercase ASCII-letter
names, possibly empty and with repeats; missing catalog names are allowed.

records.build_catalog uses schema.Schema.validate on the whole row list. Every
key must match one or more lowercase letters a through z, without normalization.
An invalid key rejects the whole input: return None on schema.SchemaError.
Otherwise return exactly {"keys": [...], "values": [...]}. Each distinct key
occurs once in keys, ordered by its FIRST occurrence in rows. Its aligned value
is from its LAST occurrence. Preserve JSON scalar types exactly, including the
difference between false, 0 and null. Empty rows returns both lists empty and
is valid. This is a pure per-call product, with no state carried between calls.

report.catalog_rows must consume records.build_catalog and return
{"ok": true, "rows": [{"key": key, "value": value}, ...]} in catalog order.
On None return {"ok": false, "rows": []}.

query.lookup_many must consume records.build_catalog and return ok true with
matches in query-key order, preserving repeated queries. Each match is exactly
{"key": query, "found": boolean, "value": latest value or null when absent}.
A present null has found true; a missing key has found false. On rejected rows
return {"ok": false, "matches": []}, even if query keys is empty.

For rows [{"key": "b", "value": 1}, {"key": "a", "value": false},
{"key": "b", "value": null}], the catalog is keys ["b", "a"], values [null,false].
The table preserves that order. Query ["b", "x", "a", "b"] keeps those four
entries: b is found with null, x is absent with null, a is found with false, and
b is found with null again. All empty-input combinations retain these rules.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# Use one stable catalog for table and lookup views

Deliver records.build_catalog(rows), report.catalog_rows(rows), and
query.lookup_many(rows, keys). The table and lookup views must call and consume
the same records.build_catalog product, not separately rebuild its semantics.
No member or role is assigned to any module.

rows is a list of dictionaries with exactly key (an ASCII string) and value
(a JSON string, integer, boolean or null). These shapes and value types are
guaranteed; floats and other shapes are outside the domain. A key may be an
invalid name. Query keys is a list of valid nonempty lowercase ASCII-letter
names, possibly empty and with repeats; missing catalog names are allowed.

records.build_catalog uses schema.Schema.validate on the whole row list. Every
key must match one or more lowercase letters a through z, without normalization.
An invalid key rejects the whole input: return None on schema.SchemaError.
Otherwise return exactly {"keys": [...], "values": [...]}. Each distinct key
occurs once in keys, ordered by its FIRST occurrence in rows. Its aligned value
is from its LAST occurrence. Preserve JSON scalar types exactly, including the
difference between false, 0 and null. Empty rows returns both lists empty and
is valid. This is a pure per-call product, with no state carried between calls.

report.catalog_rows must consume records.build_catalog and return
{"ok": true, "rows": [{"key": key, "value": value}, ...]} in catalog order.
On None return {"ok": false, "rows": []}.

query.lookup_many must consume records.build_catalog and return ok true with
matches in query-key order, preserving repeated queries. Each match is exactly
{"key": query, "found": boolean, "value": latest value or null when absent}.
A present null has found true; a missing key has found false. On rejected rows
return {"ok": false, "matches": []}, even if query keys is empty.

For rows [{"key": "b", "value": 1}, {"key": "a", "value": false},
{"key": "b", "value": null}], the catalog is keys ["b", "a"], values [null,false].
The table preserves that order. Query ["b", "x", "a", "b"] keeps those four
entries: b is found with null, x is absent with null, a is found with false, and
b is found with null again. All empty-input combinations retain these rules.

import re
from schema import And, Or, Schema, SchemaError


def build_catalog(rows):
    name = And(str, lambda value: re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", value) is not None)
    try:
        validated = Schema([{"key": name, "value": Or(str, int, bool, type(None))}]).validate(rows)
    except SchemaError:
        return None
    keys, values = [], []
    # Track first occurrence order of keys
    first_occurrence_order = []
    # Track last occurrence of each key
    last_values = {}
    
    for row in validated:
        key = row["key"]
        value = row["value"]
        
        # Track first occurrence order
        if key not in last_values:
            first_occurrence_order.append(key)
        
        # Always update to last value
        last_values[key] = value
    
    # Build keys list in first occurrence order
    keys = first_occurrence_order
    # Build values list aligned with keys
    values = [last_values[key] for key in keys]
    
    return {"keys": keys, "values": values}

"""
records.py - Record catalog and lookup operations.

This module provides functions for building catalogs from rows of key-value
pairs and performing lookups. The catalog maintains keys in first-occurrence
order, with values from the last occurrence of each key.
"""

import json
from schema import Schema, SchemaError


def build_catalog(rows):
    """
    Build a catalog from rows of key-value pairs.
    
    Args:
        rows: List of dicts with exactly 'key' and 'value' fields.
        
    Returns:
        Dict with 'keys' (list of keys in first-occurrence order) and
        'values' (list of values aligned with keys, from last occurrence).
        Returns None on schema validation error.
    """
    # Validate the schema first on the whole row list
    row_schema = Schema({
        'key': str,
        'value': (str, int, bool, type(None))
    }, strict=True)
    
    try:
        row_schema.validate(rows)
    except SchemaError:
        return None
    
    # If no rows, return empty catalog
    if not rows:
        return {'keys': [], 'values': []}
    
    # Build catalog in first-occurrence order
    seen_keys = []
    key_values = {}
    
    for row in rows:
        key = row['key']
        value = row['value']
        
        # Add key on first occurrence
        if key not in seen_keys:
            seen_keys.append(key)
            key_values[key] = []  # List to store all values for this key
        
        # Append value (will use last one)
        key_values[key].append(value)
    
    # Build result with values from last occurrence
    keys = seen_keys
    values = [key_values[key][-1] for key in keys]
    
    return {'keys': keys, 'values': values}


def catalog_rows(rows):
    """
    Convert a catalog into a list of {key, value} objects.
    
    Args:
        rows: List of dicts with exactly 'key' and 'value' fields.
        
    Returns:
        Dict with 'ok' (bool) and 'rows' (list of {key, value} dicts).
        On None return {'ok': False, 'rows': []}.
    """
    catalog = build_catalog(rows)
    if catalog is None:
        return {'ok': False, 'rows': []}
    
    result = []
    for i, key in enumerate(catalog['keys']):
        result.append({
            'key': key,
            'value': catalog['values'][i]
        })
    
    return {'ok': True, 'rows': result}


def lookup_many(rows, keys):
    """
    Look up multiple keys in a catalog.
    
    Args:
        rows: List of dicts with exactly 'key' and 'value' fields.
        keys: List of query keys (valid nonempty lowercase ASCII letters).
        
    Returns:
        Dict with 'ok' (bool) and 'matches' (list of {key, found, value} dicts).
        On schema error or rejected rows, returns {'ok': False, 'matches': []}.
    """
    catalog = build_catalog(rows)
    if catalog is None:
        return {'ok': False, 'matches': []}
    
    # Build a set of valid keys for quick lookup
    key_set = set(catalog['keys'])
    key_value_map = {}
    for i, key in enumerate(catalog['keys']):
        key_value_map[key] = catalog['values'][i]
    
    matches = []
    for query_key in keys:
        # Check if key is valid (nonempty, lowercase letters only)
        if not (1 <= len(query_key) <= 32 and all(c.islower() and c.isalpha() for c in query_key)):
            matches.append({
                'key': query_key,
                'found': False,
                'value': None
            })
            continue
        
        found = query_key in key_set
        value = key_value_map.get(query_key, None)
        
        matches.append({
            'key': query_key,
            'found': found,
            'value': value
        })
    
    return {'ok': True, 'matches': matches}

from schema import And, Or, Schema, SchemaError


def build_catalog(rows):
    name = And(str, lambda value: re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", value) is not None)
    try:
        validated = Schema([{"key": name, "value": Or(str, int, bool, type(None))}]).validate(rows)
    except SchemaError:
        return None
    keys, values = [], []
    # Track first occurrence order of keys
    first_occurrence_order = []
    # Track last occurrence of each key
    last_values = {}
    
    for row in validated:
        key = row["key"]
        value = row["value"]
        
        # Track first occurrence order
        if key not in last_values:
            first_occurrence_order.append(key)
        
        # Always update to last value
        last_values[key] = value
    
    # Build keys list in first occurrence order
    keys = first_occurrence_order
    # Build values list aligned with keys
    values = [last_values[key] for key in keys]
    
    return {"keys": keys, "values": values}

"""
records.py - Record catalog and lookup operations.

This module provides functions for building catalogs from rows of key-value
pairs and performing lookups. The catalog maintains keys in first-occurrence
order, with values from the last occurrence of each key.
"""

import json
from schema import Schema, SchemaError


def build_catalog(rows):
    """
    Build a catalog from rows of key-value pairs.
    
    Args:
        rows: List of dicts with exactly 'key' and 'value' fields.
        
    Returns:
        Dict with 'keys' (list of keys in first-occurrence order) and
        'values' (list of values aligned with keys, from last occurrence).
        Returns None on schema validation error.
    """
    # Validate the schema first on the whole row list
    row_schema = Schema({
        'key': str,
        'value': (str, int, bool, type(None))
    }, strict=True)
    
    try:
        row_schema.validate(rows)
    except SchemaError:
        return None
    
    # If no rows, return empty catalog
    if not rows:
        return {'keys': [], 'values': []}
    
    # Build catalog in first-occurrence order
    seen_keys = []
    key_values = {}
    
    for row in rows:
        key = row['key']
        value = row['value']
        
        # Add key on first occurrence
        if key not in seen_keys:
            seen_keys.append(key)
            key_values[key] = []  # List to store all values for this key
        
        # Append value (will use last one)
        key_values[key].append(value)
    
    # Build result with values from last occurrence
    keys = seen_keys
    values = [key_values[key][-1] for key in keys]
    
    return {'keys': keys, 'values': values}


def catalog_rows(rows):
    """
    Convert a catalog into a list of {key, value} objects.
    
    Args:
        rows: List of dicts with exactly 'key' and 'value' fields.
        
    Returns:
        Dict with 'ok' (bool) and 'rows' (list of {key, value} dicts).
        On None return {'ok': False, 'rows': []}.
    """
    catalog = build_catalog(rows)
    if catalog is None:
        return {'ok': False, 'rows': []}
    
    result = []
    for i, key in enumerate(catalog['keys']):
        result.append({
            'key': key,
            'value': catalog['values'][i]
        })
    
    return {'ok': True, 'rows': result}


def lookup_many(rows, keys):
    """
    Look up multiple keys in a catalog.
    
    Args:
        rows: List of dicts with exactly 'key' and 'value' fields.
        keys: List of query keys (valid nonempty lowercase ASCII letters).
        
    Returns:
        Dict with 'ok' (bool) and 'matches' (list of {key, found, value} dicts).
        On schema error or rejected rows, returns {'ok': False, 'matches': []}.
    """
    catalog = build_catalog(rows)
    if catalog is None:
        return {'ok': False, 'matches': []}
    
    # Build a set of valid keys for quick lookup
    key_set = set(catalog['keys'])
    key_value_map = {}
    for i, key in enumerate(catalog['keys']):
        key_value_map[key] = catalog['values'][i]
    
    matches = []
    for query_key in keys:
        # Check if key is valid (nonempty, lowercase letters only)
        if not (1 <= len(query_key) <= 32 and all(c.islower() and c.isalpha() for c in query_key)):
            matches.append({
                'key': query_key,
                'found': False,
                'value': None
            })
            continue
        
        found = query_key in key_set
        value = key_value_map.get(query_key, None)
        
        matches.append({
            'key': query_key,
            'found': found,
            'value': value
        })
    
    return {'ok': True, 'matches': matches}

source_contract.public_requirements:
# Use one stable catalog for table and lookup views

Deliver records.build_catalog(rows), report.catalog_rows(rows), and
query.lookup_many(rows, keys). The table and lookup views must call and consume
the same records.build_catalog product, not separately rebuild its semantics.
No member or role is assigned to any module.

rows is a list of dictionaries with exactly key (an ASCII string) and value
(a JSON string, integer, boolean or null). These shapes and value types are
guaranteed; floats and other shapes are outside the domain. A key may be an
invalid name. Query keys is a list of valid nonempty lowercase ASCII-letter
names, possibly empty and with repeats; missing catalog names are allowed.

records.build_catalog uses schema.Schema.validate on the whole row list. Every
key must match one or more lowercase letters a through z, without normalization.
An invalid key rejects the whole input: return None on schema.SchemaError.
Otherwise return exactly {"keys": [...], "values": [...]}. Each distinct key
occurs once in keys, ordered by its FIRST occurrence in rows. Its aligned value
is from its LAST occurrence. Preserve JSON scalar types exactly, including the
difference between false, 0 and null. Empty rows returns both lists empty and
is valid. This is a pure per-call product, with no state carried between calls.

report.catalog_rows must consume records.build_catalog and return
{"ok": true, "rows": [{"key": key, "value": value}, ...]} in catalog order.
On None return {"ok": false, "rows": []}.

query.lookup_many must consume records.build_catalog and return ok true with
matches in query-key order, preserving repeated queries. Each match is exactly
{"key": query, "found": boolean, "value": latest value or null when absent}.
A present null has found true; a missing key has found false. On rejected rows
return {"ok": false, "matches": []}, even if query keys is empty.

For rows [{"key": "b", "value": 1}, {"key": "a", "value": false},

import re
from schema import And, Or, Schema, SchemaError


def build_catalog(rows):
    name = And(str, lambda value: re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", value) is not None)
    try:
        validated = Schema([{"key": name, "value": Or(str, int, bool, type(None))}]).validate(rows)
    except SchemaError:
        return None
    
    # Track the order from the original input
    first_occurrence_order = []
    last_values = {}
    
    # Iterate through validated rows (schema may have reordered them)
    # But we need to track first occurrence from the ORIGINAL input order
    # So we validate each row individually and track order
    
    # Actually, let's just iterate through validated and track order
    # The schema should preserve order, but let's be safe
    for row in validated:
        key = row["key"]
        value = row["value"]
        
        # If this is the first time we see this key in our iteration, add it
        if key not in last_values:
            first_occurrence_order.append(key)
        
        # Always update the last value for this key
        last_values[key] = value
    
    # Build the result with keys in first-occurrence order
    keys = first_occurrence_order
    values = [last_values[key] for key in first_occurrence_order]
    
    return {"keys": keys, "values": values}

source_contract.public_requirements:
# Use one stable catalog for table and lookup views

Deliver records.build_catalog(rows), report.catalog_rows(rows), and
query.lookup_many(rows, keys). The table and lookup views must call and consume
the same records.build_catalog product, not separately rebuild its semantics.
No member or role is assigned to any module.

rows is a list of dictionaries with exactly key (an ASCII string) and value
(a JSON string, integer, boolean or null). These shapes and value types are
guaranteed; floats and other shapes are outside the domain. A key may be an
invalid name. Query keys is a list of valid nonempty lowercase ASCII-letter
names, possibly empty and with repeats; missing catalog names are allowed.

records.build_catalog uses schema.Schema.validate on the whole row list. Every
key must match one or more lowercase letters a through z, without normalization.
An invalid key rejects the whole input: return None on schema.SchemaError.
Otherwise return exactly {"keys": [...], "values": [...]}. Each distinct key
occurs once in keys, ordered by its FIRST occurrence in rows. Its aligned value
is from its LAST occurrence. Preserve JSON scalar types exactly, including the
difference between false, 0 and null. Empty rows returns both lists empty and
is valid. This is a pure per-call product, with no state carried between calls.

report.catalog_rows must consume records.build_catalog and return
{"ok": true, "rows": [{"key": key, "value": value}, ...]} in catalog order.
On None return {"ok": false, "rows": []}.

query.lookup_many must consume records.build_catalog and return ok true with
matches in query-key order, preserving repeated queries. Each match is exactly
{"key": query, "found": boolean, "value": latest value or null when absent}.
A present null has found true; a missing key has found false. On rejected rows
return {"ok": false, "matches": []}, even if query keys is empty.

For rows [{"key": "b", "value": 1}, {"key": "a", "value": false},
{"key": "b", "value": null}], the catalog is keys ["b", "a"], values [null,false].
The table preserves that order. Query ["b", "x", "a", "b"] keeps those four
entries: b is found with null, x is absent with null, a is found with false, and
b is found with null again. All empty-input combinations retain these rules.

# Work and acceptance

This is one immutable root goal, not a list of execution tasks. Equal members
have the same public materials and tools and start with private copies and an
empty task board. Choose your own work organization. A single member may finish
the whole contract; no communication, role split, recruitment, minimum task
count or editing order is required. Direct work may be published with
fix_patch(task_ids=[]). Named task bindings require actual ownership.

Only the declared application modules and test_member.py are editable. The
pinned schema library, this contract and test_visible.py are read-only. Public
checks contain stated examples and a bounded original API regression. Private
checks use different inputs within this same declared domain, not a different
contract. No behavior outside the stated input domain is assessed. All output
keys, scalar types, list order, duplicates and caller-input preservation are
part of the contract. Never mutate arguments, even on rejection. Use the actual
schema API and consume the stated shared product, not dummy calls or duplicate
substitute implementations. API-use observations are finite executed witnesses.

Run public tests on the current version, fix that same version, and actively
submit_integration. A fixed submission is not independent acceptance. There is
no CLI, network, persistent service or external producer. This is a named handoff-state variant of an already-used project-authored
organization-development root, not a new source benchmark. The existing branch
and any initial public diagnostics are environment preparation, not work or
discoveries already performed by current members. Training and independent
confirmation are outside this task purpose.

# Use one stable catalog for table and lookup views

Deliver records.build_catalog(rows), report.catalog_rows(rows), and
query.lookup_many(rows, keys). The table and lookup views must call and consume
the same records.build_catalog product, not separately rebuild its semantics.
No member or role is assigned to any module.

rows is a list of dictionaries with exactly key (an ASCII string) and value
(a JSON string, integer, boolean or null). These shapes and value types are
guaranteed; floats and other shapes are outside the domain. A key may be an
invalid name. Query keys is a list of valid nonempty lowercase ASCII-letter
names, possibly empty and with repeats; missing catalog names are allowed.

records.build_catalog uses schema.Schema.validate on the whole row list. Every
key must match one or more lowercase letters a through z, without normalization.
An invalid key rejects the whole input: return None on schema.SchemaError.
Otherwise return exactly {"keys": [...], "values": [...]}. Each distinct key
occurs once in keys, ordered by its FIRST occurrence in rows. Its aligned value
is from its LAST occurrence. Preserve JSON scalar types exactly, including the
difference between false, 0 and null. Empty rows returns both lists empty and
is valid. This is a pure per-call product, with no state carried between calls.

report.catalog_rows must consume records.build_catalog and return
{"ok": true, "rows": [{"key": key, "value": value}, ...]} in catalog order.
On None return {"ok": false, "rows": []}.

query.lookup_many must consume records.build_catalog and return ok true with
matches in query-key order, preserving repeated queries. Each match is exactly
{"key": query, "found": boolean, "value": latest value or null when absent}.
A present null has found true; a missing key has found false. On rejected rows
return {"ok": false, "matches": []}, even if query keys is empty.

For rows [{"key": "b", "value": 1}, {"key": "a", "value": false},
{"key": "b", "value": null}], the catalog is keys ["b", "a"], values [null,false].
The table preserves that order. Query ["b", "x", "a", "b"] keeps those four
entries: b is found with null, x is absent with null, a is found with false, and
b is found with null again. All empty-input combinations retain these rules.

import re
from schema import And, Or, Schema, SchemaError


def build_catalog(rows):
    name = And(str, lambda value: re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", value) is not None)
    try:
        validated = Schema([{"key": name, "value": Or(str, int, bool, type(None))}]).validate(rows)
    except SchemaError:
        return None
    keys, values = [], []
    # Track first occurrence order of keys
    first_occurrence_order = []
    # Track last occurrence of each key
    last_values = {}
    
    for row in validated:
        key = row["key"]
        value = row["value"]
        
        # Track first occurrence order
        if key not in last_values:
            first_occurrence_order.append(key)
        
        # Always update to last value
        last_values[key] = value
    
    # Build keys list in first occurrence order
    keys = first_occurrence_order
    # Build values list aligned with keys
    values = [last_values[key] for key in keys]
    
    return {"keys": keys, "values": values}

"""
records.py - Record catalog and lookup operations.

This module provides functions for building catalogs from rows of key-value
pairs and performing lookups. The catalog maintains keys in first-occurrence
order, with values from the last occurrence of each key.
"""

import json
from schema import Schema, SchemaError


def build_catalog(rows):
    """
    Build a catalog from rows of key-value pairs.
    
    Args:
        rows: List of dicts with exactly 'key' and 'value' fields.
        
    Returns:
        Dict with 'keys' (list of keys in first-occurrence order) and
        'values' (list of values aligned with keys, from last occurrence).
        Returns None on schema validation error.
    """
    # Validate the schema first on the whole row list
    row_schema = Schema({
        'key': str,
        'value': (str, int, bool, type(None))
    }, strict=True)
    
    try:
        row_schema.validate(rows)
    except SchemaError:
        return None
    
    # If no rows, return empty catalog
    if not rows:
        return {'keys': [], 'values': []}
    
    # Build catalog in first-occurrence order
    seen_keys = []
    key_values = {}
    
    for row in rows:
        key = row['key']
        value = row['value']
        
        # Add key on first occurrence
        if key not in seen_keys:
            seen_keys.append(key)
            key_values[key] = []  # List to store all values for this key
        
        # Append value (will use last one)
        key_values[key].append(value)
    
    # Build result with values from last occurrence
    keys = seen_keys
    values = [key_values[key][-1] for key in keys]
    
    return {'keys': keys, 'values': values}


def catalog_rows(rows):
    """
    Convert a catalog into a list of {key, value} objects.
    
    Args:
        rows: List of dicts with exactly 'key' and 'value' fields.
        
    Returns:
        Dict with 'ok' (bool) and 'rows' (list of {key, value} dicts).
        On None return {'ok': False, 'rows': []}.
    """
    catalog = build_catalog(rows)
    if catalog is None:
        return {'ok': False, 'rows': []}
    
    result = []
    for i, key in enumerate(catalog['keys']):
        result.append({
            'key': key,
            'value': catalog['values'][i]
        })
    
    return {'ok': True, 'rows': result}


def lookup_many(rows, keys):
    """
    Look up multiple keys in a catalog.
    
    Args:
        rows: List of dicts with exactly 'key' and 'value' fields.
        keys: List of query keys (valid nonempty lowercase ASCII letters).
        
    Returns:
        Dict with 'ok' (bool) and 'matches' (list of {key, found, value} dicts).
        On schema error or rejected rows, returns {'ok': False, 'matches': []}.
    """
    catalog = build_catalog(rows)
    if catalog is None:
        return {'ok': False, 'matches': []}
    
    # Build a set of valid keys for quick lookup
    key_set = set(catalog['keys'])
    key_value_map = {}
    for i, key in enumerate(catalog['keys']):
        key_value_map[key] = catalog['values'][i]
    
    matches = []
    for query_key in keys:
        # Check if key is valid (nonempty, lowercase letters only)
        if not (1 <= len(query_key) <= 32 and all(c.islower() and c.isalpha() for c in query_key)):
            matches.append({
                'key': query_key,
                'found': False,
                'value': None
            })
            continue
        
        found = query_key in key_set
        value = key_value_map.get(query_key, None)
        
        matches.append({
            'key': query_key,
            'found': found,
            'value': value
        })
    
    return {'ok': True, 'matches': matches}

# Use one stable catalog for table and lookup views

Deliver records.build_catalog(rows), report.catalog_rows(rows), and
query.lookup_many(rows, keys). The table and lookup views must call and consume
the same records.build_catalog product, not separately rebuild its semantics.
No member or role is assigned to any module.

rows is a list of dictionaries with exactly key (an ASCII string) and value
(a JSON string, integer, boolean or null). These shapes and value types are
guaranteed; floats and other shapes are outside the domain. A key may be an
invalid name. Query keys is a list of valid nonempty lowercase ASCII-letter
names, possibly empty and with repeats; missing catalog names are allowed.

records.build_catalog uses schema.Schema.validate on the whole row list. Every
key must match one or more lowercase letters a through z, without normalization.
An invalid key rejects the whole input: return None on schema.SchemaError.
Otherwise return exactly {"keys": [...], "values": [...]}. Each distinct key
occurs once in keys, ordered by its FIRST occurrence in rows. Its aligned value
is from its LAST occurrence. Preserve JSON scalar types exactly, including the
difference between false, 0 and null. Empty rows returns both lists empty and
is valid. This is a pure per-call product, with no state carried between calls.

report.catalog_rows must consume records.build_catalog and return
{"ok": true, "rows": [{"key": key, "value": value}, ...]} in catalog order.
On None return {"ok": false, "rows": []}.

query.lookup_many must consume records.build_catalog and return ok true with
matches in query-key order, preserving repeated queries. Each match is exactly
{"key": query, "found": boolean, "value": latest value or null when absent}.
A present null has found true; a missing key has found false. On rejected rows
return {"ok": false, "matches": []}, even if query keys is empty.

For rows [{"key": "b", "value": 1}, {"key": "a", "value": false},
{"key": "b", "value": null}], the catalog is keys ["b", "a"], values [null,false].
The table preserves that order. Query ["b", "x", "a", "b"] keeps those four
entries: b is found with null, x is absent with null, a is found with false, and
b is found with null again. All empty-input combinations retain these rules.

cost.scope: All recorded work, including unsuccessful and technically unknown episodes. Totals are partial when indicated; absent token usage and held reservations are never inferred as actual tokens. Initial environment diagnostics remain separate from member work, nested within worker time.

environment_preparation.scope: Actual recorded preparation executions and cache reuse only. Never member discoveries or extra learner calls; preparation wall times are nested in worker occupancy.

first_block_gate.scope: Mechanism-only gate: does not condition on reward, messaging, births, or collaboration success.

scope: Two handoff development variants, four paired evidence/framing conditions, two seeds. Initial preparation is not model work; explicit team framing is a prompt intervention. No independent benchmark claim, causal contribution credit or parameter-learning gain. All 16 original slots retained.
